items.title: 9.1 Bronsted-Lowry concept (acid aur base ki Bronsted-Lowry pehchan) (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of the chapter opening and topic 9.1 with Table 9.1, printed pages 189-191.

blocks.text: Experimental (tajurbe wali) chemistry ke shuru se hi scientists acids aur bases ko un ki khaas properties (khoobiyon) se pehchante aaye hain. Acids ka taste (zaiqa) sour (khatta) hota hai aur bases bitter (karwe) hote hain. Acids aur bases kuch dyes (rang dene wali cheezon) ka colour bhi badalte hain jinhen indicators kehte hain, jaise litmus aur phenolphthalein. Acids litmus ko blue se red karte hain aur basic phenolphthalein ko pink se colourless (be-rang). Bases litmus ko red se blue aur phenolphthalein ko colourless se pink karte hain. In colour changes se pata chalta hai ke acids aur bases ek doosre ko neutralize (ek doosre ka asar khatam) karte hain. Neutralization mein acids aur bases react kar ke ionic substances banate hain jinhen salts kehte hain.

blocks.title: Interesting Information (dilchasp maloomat)
blocks.text: Stomach (maida) ki acidity (tezabiyat) zyada HCl ki wajah se hoti hai. Is ka ilaj halke (mild) bases, jaise baking soda, le kar kiya jata hai. (Kitab ka box yahin khatam ho jata hai.)

1923 mein Danish chemist J.N. Bronsted aur English chemist T.M. Lowry ne alag alag Arrhenius theory ko aage barhaya. Arrhenius theory ki limitation (kami) yeh hai ke woh acid aur base ka reaction sirf pani (aqueous medium) mein explain karti hai, jabke bohat se reactions pani ke ilawa doosre solvents mein ya baghair kisi solvent ke hote hain. Bronsted-Lowry ne bataya ke acid-base reactions ko proton-transfer (proton ka ek se doosre ko jana) reactions samjha ja sakta hai, aur acids aur bases ki definition (tareef) isi proton (H⁺) ke transfer se ki ja sakti hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein “Arhenius” chhapa hai; sahi spelling Arrhenius hai.

blocks.title: Bronsted–Lowry acid aur base
blocks.text: Bronsted–Lowry concept ke mutabiq acid woh species hai jo proton-transfer reaction mein proton deti hai (donor), aur base woh species hai jo proton leti hai (acceptor).

Jab HCl pani mein dissolve hota (ghulta) hai to ek H⁺ ion (proton) HCl se pani ko chala jata hai. Yeh O atom ke lone pair (akela electron pair) se jur kar H₃O⁺ banata hai. Yani HCl (acid) ne H⁺ diya aur H₂O (base) ne use liya.

blocks.text_alt: HCl(g) [Proton donor] + H₂O(ℓ) [Proton acceptor] ⇌ H₃O⁺(aq) [Conjugate acid] + Cl⁻(aq) [Conjugate base]

blocks.title: Conjugate acid
blocks.text: Jab Bronsted base acid se proton le leta hai to jo species banti hai use conjugate acid kehte hain.
Hydronium ion (H₃O⁺) pani ka conjugate acid hai.

blocks.title: Conjugate base
blocks.text: Jab acid base ko proton de deta hai to jo species bachti hai use conjugate base kehte hain.
HCl-Cl⁻ aur H₂O-H₃O⁺ conjugate acid-base pairs (jore) hain.

Jab ammonia pani mein dissolve hoti hai to bhi proton transfer hota hai. H₂O ka ek H⁺ N atom ke lone pair se jurta hai, aur NH₄⁺ aur OH⁻ bante hain. Ek H⁺ kam hone se pani ka molecule OH⁻ ion ban jata hai:

blocks.text_alt: NH₃(g) [Base] + H₂O(ℓ) [Acid] ⇌ OH⁻(aq) [Conjugate base] + NH₄⁺(aq) [Conjugate acid]

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ne NH₄⁺ ke neeche “Conjugate base” likha hai. NH₄⁺ tab banta hai jab base NH₃ proton leta hai, is liye NH₄⁺ NH₃ ka conjugate acid hai; yahan conjugate base sirf OH⁻ hai.
Is reaction mein H₂O (acid) ne proton diya aur NH₃ (base) ne liya. NH₃-NH₄⁺ aur H₂O-OH⁻ conjugate acid-base pairs hain.
In examples se pata chalta hai ke H₂O amphoteric hai: ek reaction mein base ka kaam karta hai aur doosre mein acid ka.

blocks.title: Amphoteric substance
blocks.text: Amphoteric substance woh species hai jo doosre reactant ke mutabiq acid bhi ban sakti hai aur base bhi (proton de bhi sakti hai aur le bhi sakti hai).
Bronsted-Lowry theory pani ke ilawa doosre solvents mein, balke baghair solvent ke reactions par bhi apply hoti hai. Ammonia gas aur HCl gas react kar ke solid NH₄Cl banati hain.
Is reaction mein HCl acid hai kyunke woh NH₃ molecule ko proton deta hai. NH₃ base hai, halanke yahan hydroxide ion OH⁻ maujood hi nahi; woh HCl se proton leta hai.

blocks.title: Asaan alfaaz mein
blocks.text: Har pair mein do species hoti hain jin mein sirf ek H⁺ ka farq hota hai. Jis ke paas H⁺ zyada hai woh acid (ya conjugate acid), aur jis ke paas ek H⁺ kam hai woh base (ya conjugate base). Example: HCl aur Cl⁻, H₃O⁺ aur H₂O, NH₄⁺ aur NH₃.

blocks.caption: Table 9.1 Aam species ke conjugate acid-base pairs

items: Acids sour (khatte), bases bitter (karwe); dono indicators ka rang badalte hain aur neutralization se salts banate hain.
Bronsted-Lowry (1923): acid = proton dene wala, base = proton lene wala. Arrhenius theory sirf pani tak limited (mehdood) thi.
Base + H⁺ = conjugate acid; acid − H⁺ = conjugate base: HCl/Cl⁻, H₂O/H₃O⁺, NH₃/NH₄⁺, H₂O/OH⁻.
Pani amphoteric hai; theory baghair solvent ke bhi lagti hai: HCl(g) + NH₃(g) → NH₄Cl(s).
